finalText:
Merge keeps both branches' history intact. It adds one new commit that ties the two together. Nothing already recorded ever changes.

Rebase takes your commits and replays them on top of the other branch. That makes history look like a straight line. But every replayed commit gets a new ID.

Merge is safe anytime, especially on branches other people share. Rebase is best kept to your own work, before anyone else has pulled it.

One rule matters most: never rebase commits you've already pushed to somewhere others can see.
